subject: Re: Data erasure sampling protocol and automation playbook
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@hyperionfin.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Hyperion Compliance <compliance@hyperionfin.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Data erasure samples for SOC 2 audit - requirements

Naomi,

Our SOC 2 auditor has asked that we obtain a reproducible sampling artefact demonstrating tenant data erasure for a random subset of tenants across your platform. They specifically want:

- Description of the sampling methodology (how tenants are selected, RNG/seed, percentage)
- The automation logs or runbook that executed the erasure for the sampled tenants
- Hashlists or manifests showing before/after states and checksums
- Timeline for when we can receive artifacts and whether artifacts can be time-stamped and signed

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated delivery date? We're aiming to include this in our control evidence bundle for the week of Nov 22.

Thanks,
Sarah Bennett
Senior Compliance Manager
Hyperion Financial

--
Attachment: auditor_request_summary.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@hyperionfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data erasure samples for SOC 2 audit - requirements

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can provide a reproducible sampling packet that includes the selection seed, manifests, and signed automation run logs. High level plan below, attaching the playbook and automation runbook for review.

What we'll deliver (initial package):
- erasure_sampling_playbook_v1.pdf: methodology, statistical rationale, and mapping to SOC 2 CC6.1/ISO A.14 controls
- automation_runbook.md: step-by-step automation flow, guarded rollback checks, idempotency notes
- sample_output_manifest.csv: sample of before/after file hashes, tenant id, timestamp, and retention TTL references
- signed run logs: logs produced by our erasure automation, signed with our internal key and timestamped (we'll redact token-level data)

Sampling methodology (summary):
- Random stratified sampling by tenant size bucket (small/medium/large) to avoid bias; default sample rate 1% of active tenants with min 5 tenants per bucket
- RNG: HMAC_DRBG seeded with the UTC date + org-wide seed (we will include the seed and the exact command used to generate the indices)
- Reproducibility: the playbook contains the exact SQL and CLI commands used to extract the candidate list; we'll provide a script that auditors can run against a read-only snapshot to reproduce the selection

Data artifacts and proofs:
- Pre-erasure snapshot hashes (sha256) for selected objects
- Post-erasure manifests showing non-recoverability markers and object tombstones where applicable
- System-level audit trail entry (immutable) referencing the run id and signature

Delivery timeline:
- Draft package to Hyperion for review: Thu, 2026-11-12 EOD (PST)
- Final signed artifacts (after your review) by Tue, 2026-11-23

A couple of questions for scope alignment:
1) Do you need full object dumps, or are manifests (path + sha256) sufficient?
2) Is the auditor comfortable with our redaction approach (we always redact PII and tokens but provide full structural metadata)?

Attachments included: erasure_sampling_playbook_v1.pdf, automation_runbook.md, sample_output_manifest.csv (sample).

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--

Attachment: automation_runbook.md (text/markdown)
Attachment: sample_output_manifest.csv (text/csv)
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@hyperionfin.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data erasure samples for SOC 2 audit - requirements

Naomi — this is great, thanks. A few clarifying items from the auditor after a quick pass through the playbook: 

- Sample size: they asked whether 1% with min 5 per bucket is derived from a power calculation; can you include the power calculation or rationale in the next version?
- Timestamping: they prefer artifacts that include an RFC3339 timestamp and are signed with a key that can be traced to the vendor's KMS. Can you confirm your signing process?
- Evidence retention: will the artifacts you hand us be retained anywhere on your side after delivery (we need to document custody)?

If you can include the additional details and the signing certificate chain (or CA reference), we should be good. Also, is the reproducibility script safe to run against a read-only snapshot without exposing production credentials?

Best,
Sarah

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can provide a reproducible sampling packet...
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@hyperionfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data erasure samples for SOC 2 audit - requirements

Sarah — quick follow up addressing the auditor's clarifying questions. Summary of changes and answers: 

1) Sample size rationale: added a short power calculation appendix to the playbook (section 4.2). Short version: with our tenant distribution the 1% rate yields >95% confidence to detect a systemic failure with assumed defect rate >=2% at 95% power; we also include an escalation threshold if any sampled tenant shows evidence of incomplete erasure.

2) Signing and timestamps:
- Artifacts will be signed using a KMS-backed RSA key via our signing service (kms-sign-v2). Each artifact includes an RFC3339 timestamp and a detached signature file (.sig).
- We will provide the certificate fingerprint and the KMS key id. If you require the full cert chain we can export the signing cert and include CA references in the bundle.

3) Evidence custody and retention:
- Delivered artifacts are intended for transfer to your compliance storage. We will retain a minimal indexed record (run id, hash of the artifact, timestamp) for 90 days to support auditor follow-ups, after which the index entries are purged per our retention policy. We will not retain full payloads unless explicitly requested and contracted.

4) Reproducibility script safety: the script uses a read-only snapshot endpoint and does not require privileged credentials; auditors can run it with a one-time token we generate for the snapshot. The playbook documents the exact command and the token issuance procedure.

Next steps:
- I'll upload the updated playbook (v1.1) with the power calculation appendix and sample signatures to the shared folder by EOD today.
- Draft package will remain on the timeline for Thu, 2026-11-12 EOD; final signed artifacts by Tue, 2026-11-23 once you confirm scope.

If Hyperion's auditor wants to speak directly to Karthik about the automation idempotency checks or to Kimberly about KMS signing practices, we can set a 30-minute call next week.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
